bet.text: A center of gravity so low that the driver can cross the field and the charge station without worrying about collisions or obstacles.

demand.text: Four priorities: score on the side opposite pickup, to drive less in auto; cross the charge station quickly; specialize in the double substation; fit a triple balance.
There are two double substations and one single, so a robot that uses the double one fits on more alliances.

auto.text: A three pieces plus balance auto, announced for SunDome; the arm reaches far out ("Yoshi" auto), so the robot drives less.
On the bump side the arm drops the first cube over the bump, and the robot crosses only twice.
By Houston auto ran without vision.

cycle.text: Score, drive to the double substation, take a piece and come back.
The operator sets the level, the piece and whether a cone is upright.
It was always willing to be the partner that cycles over the charge station.

endgame.text: The reveal lists auto balancing; being friendly to a triple balance was one priority for the 26 by 28 in frame.

fallback.text: A spare arm: inline connectors are used only at the arm, so that the spare can be swapped in between matches, and it needs no calibration.
A poster who was at an event says the arm was swapped during finals in about 10 minutes.

gave_up.text: Teleop floor pickup: the intake was not optimized for it, and widening it was discussed and not done.
Arm speed: even with about 10 lb of brass ballast at the front, the arm ran at about half its design rotation speed, because faster kicked the base up.

changed.text: A deployable full-width cube roller in the first concept was dropped.
Forks on the arm were planned and left out; the four motors sized for them stayed.
The drive went from L3 gearing to 16T, then 18T pinions.
Vision first ran at the district championship, in a limited way, and was retuned before the world championship.

outcome.text: 69-16-0 in official play; ranked 29 by championship OPR (68.19, Galileo).

solves.text: Cross the long field quickly, and go over the charge station in any direction faster than going around it

cost.text: At the start of the season, on standard L3, it could fill the whole grid twice on one battery; the off-season 12-motor drive, at its faster gearing, got through about two thirds of a grid before brownout protection

facts.text: Frame 26 in wide and 28 in long
SDS MK4i modules; three drive gearings in the year: standard L3, then L3 with a 16T and with an 18T pinion
Drive ratio at the end of the season (18T pinion on L3 gears)
A custom motor spacer with two hole patterns moves the motor to fit the 16T and 18T pinions
Target for crossing the charge station (caption), less than about
A tuned coefficient on angular velocity corrects the drift that came from rotating while translating
Feedforwards for path following are tuned on a long straight path with translational PID off, and were redone at every gear change
Off-season, before IRI: 12 drive motors at 4.75:1 had the same top speed as the 8-motor practice robot and gained about half a robot length by half field

solves.text: Reach about 40 in or more past the edge of the robot to score, and stow low when driving

cost.text: The steel-cord belt of the first stage broke on occasion, once in competition; no root cause was found, and hold-position current limits were adjusted
Off-season: at Chezy Champs a 3D printed e-chain mounting point at the second arm's rear bearing block failed, the cables were no longer managed and that arm stopped working

facts.text: The first stage is belt driven; Dyneema cord moves the second stage from the first stage's motion; the arm is powered both ways
Tubes: 3 in and 2.5 in square with 1/8 in wall, pocketed, and 2 in square with 1/16 in wall, not pocketed
Half-inch tube steps in place of the usual one-inch steps, because larger tube is stiffer for the same weight
The received tubing was measured and the bearing block CAD adjusted to match, so there is almost no gap
The cord is tensioned by inline chain turnbuckles; belts have no designed tensioner, only a clamp adjustable by one tooth and printed idlers that could change diameter
All belts of the extension are HTD, width
Two constant force springs only keep tension on the cable carrier
Extension waits until the shoulder is close to its target, so that the arm is not long through the swing
A plate on the middle stage is the hard stop at full extension; a cascade needs one only on the first stage

functions.name: Arm pivot

solves.text: Swing a long arm quickly, precisely and to the same place every time

cost.text: The robot does wheelies, so arm moves were coordinated to keep it on two wheels only very briefly

functions.type: chain-driven rear shoulder on a dead axle

facts.text: Reduction, roughly
The pivot is at the rear, which minimizes how far the arm has to extend to score
Four motors
Pre-stretched number 35 chain with the tensioner close to the gearbox plate, and the largest output sprocket that fit, 58 teeth
REV gears on rounded hex, for a much tighter fit than other FRC gears
Two X-contact bearings of 2.5 in inside diameter around a dead axle, which closes the top of the A-frame; the bearing set the axle diameter
The axle is 6061, machined from tube of 2.75 in outside diameter and 1/4 in wall; it stays with the arm in a swap
Motion Magic without gravity feedforward: onboard PID and the high reduction were accurate enough

functions.name: Wrist

solves.text: Add a joint at the end of the arm at low weight, without a planetary gearbox

cost.text: It had to be planned in early, because adding a wrist to a telescoping arm later would be very hard

functions.type: belt-driven wrist with its motor on the intake

facts.text: Reduction, roughly
Pulleys on the intake are driven and turn the wrist around a fixed pulley at the end of the arm
Belts in every stage except the first, with 3D printed Onyx pulleys on hex inserts
Intake and wrist weigh about, including motors
Standoffs are hard stops at both ends; one is used for zeroing

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Take cones and cubes with one light intake, including fallen cones, from the ground and the shelf

cost.text: The first roller, rubber rollers on a tube, weighed about three pounds and was replaced
Not optimized for teleop ground pickup

functions.type: dead axle roller intake for both pieces

facts.text: A cone is held between two parallel rollers and another roller handles the cube; largely inspired by the Everybot
The last roller was flipped back into the intake so that it stows lower
Rollers are McMaster 5236K255 rubber on polycarbonate tube, with printed end caps held by epoxy
The sleeves go on the tubes by floating them on air
Plates are 7075-T651, 1/4 in thick with 3/16 in ribs

functions.name: A-frame superstructure and brass bar

solves.text: Hold a long arm stiffly and keep the robot from tipping

cost.text: Rivets with steel mandrels almost never loosen but are a slight pain to drill out; once a wrong assembly order meant drilling out a bunch

functions.type: box tube A-frame with front ballast

facts.text: Stowed height, less than
Weight, about, without additional ballast as stated at the reveal
A later talk gives about 90 lb at inspection in championship form, with 10 lb of brass at the front included
The center of gravity is about four to five inches off the ground
The solid brass front rail weighs about 10 lb; in solid aluminum it would be about 3 lb
Tubes and gussets are 6061; gussets are 1/8 in thick, on both sides
Rivets sit 1/4 in from the tube edge, for stiffness and to remove material between them

solves.text: Know the arm's position with no external encoders

cost.text: Off-season: one homing button failed internally, which the team suspects came from repeated high-speed collisions; it had survived the season

facts.text: Shoulder, extension and wrist use only the motors' internal encoders
A button on the robot sets home with the arm in a known position; a controller button drives the joints into hard stops at low voltage until velocity nears zero
A second button toggles brake mode, so the arm can be put up for the start of auto
When disabled, LEDs are red, or green once the arm is home; when enabled, purple asks for a cube and yellow for a cone

functions.name: Vision and automatic cone scoring

solves.text: Line up a cone wherever it sits in the intake

cost.text: Strict thresholds kept false positives rare but cost cycle time; in many cases the driver scored faster

functions.type: AprilTag localization with time of flight cone sensing

facts.text: At Houston: two global shutter color cameras (OV9782), each on its own Orange Pi 5, running PhotonVision
A time of flight sensor on the intake's inner wall finds the center of the cone
The robot aligns sideways and in angle; the driver pulls forward to confirm; it ejects when in tolerance
Tolerance: X and Y within 1 in, yaw within 1 degree, pitch within 3 degrees of 0
Vision is trusted less with distance, by a coefficient on the distance to the closest tag

functions.name: Autonomous software

solves.text: Build and change autos quickly, with a consistent result

functions.type: PathPlanner trajectories with custom command scheduling

facts.text: Custom methods run commands in parallel or in sequence with a path, in place of PathPlanner's markers
Earlier in the season paths were joined at common control points; later independent trajectories were found more intuitive
All modules are pointed forward before the match so that no wheel turns in place at the start
On the bump side each module crosses the bump on its own, to reduce jolt and slip

functions.name: Wiring

solves.text: Keep the robot electrically reliable and the arm quick to swap

cost.text: It may take some time from programming or driver practice

functions.type: soldered wiring with connectors only at the arm

facts.text: Connectors for motor power, CAN and sensor power only at the arm; everything else is soldered
Connectors that must exist, such as roboRIO ports, are hot glued
A quick swap uses lever nuts first and is soldered when there is time

decisions.because: there are two, the piece is in a known place, and a robot that uses it fits on more alliances
decisions.instead_of: the single substation or the open field
decisions.cost: an intake not optimized for teleop ground pickup

decisions.choice: Keep the center of gravity very low
decisions.because: the driver should not have to care about collisions or obstacles

decisions.choice: A rear pivot with a telescoping arm
decisions.because: the game is about reaching out, not up, and a rear pivot minimizes the extension
decisions.instead_of: tilted elevators, a double-jointed arm or a centered pivot, which were also laid out

decisions.because: driving and accelerating faster was the bigger advantage
decisions.instead_of: more front ballast to move the arm faster
decisions.cost: an arm that ran at about half its design rotation speed

decisions.because: the structure that holds the arm has to be extremely stiff
decisions.instead_of: the parallel plates of earlier 2910 robots

decisions.choice: Number 35 chain on the arm pivot
No external encoders on the arm
decisions.because: it simplified the design, and a replacement arm needs no calibration

decisions.choice: Four motors on the arm pivot
decisions.because: forks on the arm were planned, without a shifter or a slower ratio
decisions.instead_of: two motors, which would have run fine

decisions.because: with four motors it was not needed and would only add complexity
they are lighter and much stiffer at the end of a fast arm, and there was little time when impact resistance was needed
a wider one has to be very precise to fit the double substation quickly, and a narrow one helps automated scoring
its packaging with the arm was a big challenge and it served a part of the game the team did not mean to play often

decisions.choice: PhotonVision with Arducams on Orange Pis
decisions.because: higher frame rate and lower latency, better tuning and calibration, and global shutter
wheel odometry that is consistently wrong can be adjusted for, and poor vision measurements came at random
inspection work was one of the reasons

decisions.choice: A primary geometry part in SolidWorks
decisions.because: every subsystem derives from the same layout sketches of the whole robot
